_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship), 'provisional' (romanization mine, not found outside), 'decided' (a project style call). Sections render as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored.

周恩来.cast: Founder and commander of the Party's intelligence and security work; built and directed the Central Special Section in Shanghai. Aliases include Wu Hao and, later, Hu Gong (“Old Hu”).

陈赓.cast: Chief of the Special Section's intelligence branch, working under the alias “Wang Yong.”

顾顺章.cast: Head of the Special Section's Action Section (the Red Squad); a stage magician by trade, alias “Hua Guangqi.” His 1931 defection nearly destroyed the underground Party.

李强.cast: Founder of the Party's radio-communications work; built its first transmitter. Alias “Zeng Peihong.”

蒋介石.note: The conventional English form is used, not pinyin Jiang Jieshi.

董醒吾.note: “Fat Dong” in Li Qiang's account; the personal name is given uncertainly in the source as Dong Xingwu or Dong Shengwu.

鲍罗廷.note: Mikhail Borodin, Comintern adviser to the Kuomintang.

任弼时.note: Aliases Peng Desheng and Hu Shaofu.

恽代英.note: Alias Wang Zuolin; executed in Nanjing.

马林.note: Henk Sneevliet, the Comintern's representative at the First Congress, known as Maring.

汪寿华.note: Also known as He Songlin; a leader of the Shanghai workers' uprisings, murdered in the April 12 coup.

孙子.note: The ancient strategist; the conventional English spelling Sun Tzu is kept, not pinyin Sunzi.

洪扬生.note: Chief of Section One; later renamed Hong Songtao.

熊瑾玎.note: Central accountant; ran the 'Fuxing Trading Company' front. Husband of Zhu Duansui.

周生赉.note: Western-medicine doctor who ran the Shengli Hospital.

何家兴.note: With He Zhihua, later betrayed Luo Yinong.

贺稚华.note: He Jiaxing's wife; the two betrayed Luo Yinong.

李一超.note: Alias Li Kuntai; better known as the martyr Zhao Yiman.

赵一曼.note: Real name Li Kuntai (Li Yichao); anti-Japanese martyr.

李侠.note: The underground-radio hero of the film The Unfailing Radio Waves, modeled on Li Bai.

李白.note: Party radio operator, executed 1949; the model for the film character Li Xia.

裘慧英.note: Li Bai's wife; originally named Qiu Lanfen.

潘震亚.note: Law professor and lawyer who defended arrested comrades.

费国禧.note: Lawyer used by the Special Section.

尤阿根.note: Detective chief at the Laozha police station.

鲁涤平.note: Hunan warlord in whose army Chen Geng first served.

孙中山.note: Conventional English form, not pinyin Sun Zhongshan.

杨希闵.note: Commander of the Yunnan (Dian) army that mutinied in 1925.

刘震寰.note: Commander of the Guangxi (Gui) army that mutinied in 1925.

谭曙卿.note: Third Division commander in the second Eastern Expedition.

牛惠霖.note: English-trained orthopedic surgeon; cousin of Song Qingling.

陈知非.note: Son of Chen Geng and Wang Genying.

卢冬生.note: Chen Geng's aide from the Nanchang Uprising.

陆留.note: Sent with Chen Geng and Gu Shunzhang to the USSR in 1926.

欧阳新.note: Alias Liu Dahan, nicknamed 'Big Hunk'; born surnamed Liu.

陆连奎.note: Detective chief of the British concession police; Chen Geng's landlord.

张克侠.note: Secret Party member; chief of staff to Zhang Zizhong.

董健吾.note: Underground pastor linked to the Special Section's intelligence branch.

钱大钧.note: Kuomintang Songhu garrison commander, later Jiangnan 'bandit-suppression' commander.

蒋先云.note: One of the 'Three Heroes of Whampoa.'

贺衷寒.note: One of the 'Three Heroes of Whampoa.'

阿英/钱杏村.note: Pen name of Qian Xingcun (1900–1977), the writer and literary historian.

张文.note: aka Zhang Guodong, 中统 memoirist

任卓宣.note: pen name Ye Qing 叶青

赵唯刚.cast: Instructor at the Fengtian (Shenyang) Military Academy and secretary-general of the Party's Manchuria Special Committee; a long-serving intelligence agent inside the Northeastern military establishment. Original name Zhao Shiyu.

蔡伯祥.cast: Chairman of the Manchuria Special Committee, known as the pockmarked "Manchuria Pockmark"; worked in Shenyang under cover of a hospital. Later wrongly killed as a suspected traitor and posthumously cleared.

国民党.note: The older romanization Kuomintang is kept, as is conventional in English.

中央特科.note: Zhongyang Teke; the Party's underground intelligence and security apparatus in Shanghai. Rendered “Central Special Section” throughout.

共产国际.note: The Communist International, Moscow's world body of communist parties.

红队.note: The Special Section's armed action unit, also called the “Dog-Beating Squad.”

黄埔军校.note: The Whampoa Military Academy, the Kuomintang's military academy near Guangzhou; the older romanization Whampoa is kept, and 'Whampoa' alone is used after first mention.

东方大学.en: Communist University of the Toilers of the East
东方大学.pinyin: Communist University of the Toilers of the East

中统.pinyin: Central Bureau of Investigation and Statistics

中国民权保障同盟.en: China League for the Protection of Civil Rights

广州.note: Guangzhou, not Canton (per the collection's name ledger).

海参崴.note: The Pacific port; from Shanghai the sea route to the Soviet Union.

和合坊.note: A lilong (lane-neighborhood) off Avenue Joffre in the French Concession, where Bai Xin was hidden at No. 43 and shot.

蒲石路.note: A street in the French Concession (today Changle Road, 长乐路); the North China Daily News named it in reporting the killing.

白色恐怖.note: The Kuomintang's campaign of arrests and killings against Communists and the left after 1927.

巡捕房.note: The police force of a foreign concession in Shanghai; the constables were xunbu. Rendered “concession police” (or, for a specific concession, e.g. “the French Concession police”) throughout.

租界.note: The foreign-administered concession areas of Shanghai: the French Concession and the International Settlement.

领事裁判权.note: The treaty right by which foreign nationals in China answered to their own consular courts, not to Chinese law.

龙潭三杰.note: Zhou Enlai’s name for the trio Li Kenong, Qian Zhuangfei, and Hu Di, planted at the heart of the Nationalist secret service; the “dragon pool” (longtan) evokes the tiger’s-den peril of their work.

孙子兵法.note: Sun Tzu's classic, The Art of War. The book quotes two chapters: “Attack by Stratagem” (谋攻篇) and “On the Use of Spies” (用间篇).

论反对日本帝国主义的策略.pinyin: Lun fandui Riben diguozhuyi de celue

特务工作之理论与实际.en: The Theory and Practice of Secret Service Work
特务工作之理论与实际.pinyin: The Theory and Practice of Secret Service Work

抗战以来.en: Since the War of Resistance Began
抗战以来.pinyin: Since the War of Resistance Began

字林西报.note: The leading English-language daily of the foreign settlement in Shanghai (1864–1951), published by the British.

时报.note: Shi Bao (The Eastern Times), a Shanghai daily.

申报.note: Shen Bao, the most influential Chinese-language newspaper in Republican Shanghai (1872–1949).

大陆报.note: The China Press (Chinese name Dalu Bao), an American-run English daily in Shanghai.

民国日报.note: Minguo Ribao (Republican Daily News), a Kuomintang organ.

中华英烈.note: Zhonghua Yinglie (Chinese Martyrs), a mainland journal on revolutionary martyrs.

君宪救国论.en: Saving the Nation Through Constitutional Monarchy
